examples.problem_statement: Multiply 82 × 89 using the Nikhilam base method

solution.operation: Choose the base 100
solution.description: Both numbers are near this power of 10, so Nikhilam applies

solution.operation: Write the deviations from the base
solution.description: Deviation = number − base

solution.operation: Cross-add for the left part
solution.description: Either cross-sum gives the same left part

solution.operation: Multiply the deviations for the right part
solution.description: The right part occupies 2 digits — the width of the base's zeros

solution.operation: Adjust the right part to fit the base width
solution.description: The right part cannot be wider than the base's zeros, so the excess moves into the left part — this carry is part of the method, not an afterthought

solution.operation: Assemble the answer
solution.description: left \times 100 + right, with the digits placed by width

common_mistakes: treating the product of two negative deviations as negative, when two minuses give a positive right part
writing the whole product in the right part instead of carrying the overflow into the left part

solution.description: Both numbers are near this power of 10, so Nikhilam applies

solution.operation: Write the deviations from the base
solution.description: Deviation = number − base

solution.operation: Cross-add for the left part
solution.description: Either cross-sum gives the same left part

solution.operation: Multiply the deviations for the right part
solution.description: The right part occupies 2 digits — the width of the base's zeros

solution.operation: Adjust the right part to fit the base width
solution.result: \text{the product } -27 \text{ is negative, so complete it from the base: }\;\lceil 27 \div 100 \rceil = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{left } 106 - 1 = 105,\; \text{right } 1\times100 -27 = 73
solution.description: The right part cannot be wider than the base's zeros, so the excess moves into the left part — this carry is part of the method, not an afterthought

solution.operation: Assemble the answer
solution.description: left \times 100 + right, with the digits placed by width

common_mistakes: sign error when one deviation is positive and the other negative
forgetting to complete a negative right part from the base, and to reduce the left part by the amount borrowed

solution.description: The base has 4 zeros, so the number is written with 4 digits, adding leading zeros if it is shorter — the complement is taken column by column

solution.operation: Every digit before the last non-zero one: from 9
solution.description: 'All from 9' applies to each digit up to but excluding the last non-zero digit

solution.operation: The last non-zero digit: from 10; trailing zeros stay 0
solution.description: 'The last from 10' applies to the last NON-ZERO digit; any zeros after it are already complete and stay 0 (taking 10 from a 0 would produce a two-digit column)

solution.operation: Write the column results in order
solution.description: Each column already holds a single digit, so they are read off left to right with no borrowing anywhere

common_mistakes: taking the last digit from 9 as well, giving an answer one too small
forgetting to pad a short number with leading zeros before complementing
applying 'from 10' to a trailing zero instead of the last non-zero digit
